t: A man steps out of the shadows.
His name is Nicodemus, and he is about to risk his reputation for one conversation.
This is Bible Bits, things you may have missed.
Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, a man of rank with a seat among the leaders.
Jesus himself called him a teacher of Israel.
He knew the law, he knew the scriptures, but he did not have every answer.
The leaders had made up their minds about Jesus.
So he came to Jesus at night.
Rabbi, we know you are a teacher, come from God.
Jesus answers with something he did not expect.
Nicodemus asks how a man can enter his mother's womb a second time.
Jesus explains, not a second birth of the body, a new beginning from the spirit.
No big decision, no public stand.
The Bible says nothing more of Nicodemus for some time.
Then the leaders want Jesus arrested.
In a room full of his colleagues, one voice speaks up.
Does our law judge a man before it hears him?
Two men step forward to bury him.
He brings about a hundred pounds of myrrh and allos, roughly 75 pounds today.
John even reminds us who he is, the man who first came to Jesus by night.
Now he comes in daylight, carrying the weight in front of everyone.
And that is the last the Bible tells us.
We do not know what became of him after.
